newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU abolishes grain export tax regulation.
newsitem.headline: EU abolishes grain export tax regulation.

text.p: The European Union, deciding on Thursday to scrap wheat export taxes, went even further and abolished the regulation that had brought them into force last month, EU grain officials said.
The effect of this is to lessen the threat, for those who decide to take out the new "nil value" export licences, of being hit with an unexpected return to taxation before the licences can be used.

The "nil value" licence in force from Friday is neither subsidised nor taxed, but has a short validity of 30 days and is exposed to whatever tax or subsidy happens to be in force on the day the paperwork is used against an export shipment.
However, abolishing the regulation will ease industry fears that a tax could be quickly reintroduced, since a cumbersome new regulation would be needed to do so, traders said.

Officials said earlier the "nil value" decision would most likely be an initial step towards restoring the full 4-5 month validity of wheat export licences, which could be done by turning the missing value into a zero.
This could then be fixed in value, without fear of further Commission intervention, until the end of October.
